quizzes.title: Vision and Pillars MCQ
quizzes.passage: Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget for the financial year 2026-27, which is her ninth consecutive Union Budget. The budget was prepared in a newly inaugurated building, and the government has presented it as a blueprint driven by Yuva Shakti. The budget is guided by a set of principles that the government has set out for the country's economy. The budget was tabled on a day of the week that had never before been used for a Union Budget, which made it a first for Parliament. The agenda is organised into six pillars of growth, and the pillars cover several different parts of the economy. Each pillar addresses a separate area, and together they form the core of the government's growth agenda for the coming year. The budget is a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the government for a financial year, and it is presented in Parliament. Preparing the budget involves several departments and bodies, and the presentation is one step in a longer process that the government follows each year. The budget also reflects the government's approach to growth for the coming year, as set out in its official budget material. Taken as a whole, the budget is a blueprint for the country's economic growth in the year ahead.

questions.q: On which day of the week was the Union Budget 2026-27 tabled, marking a Parliamentary first?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the first-ever Union Budget was tabled on a Sunday, a Parliamentary first.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the three Kartavyas that guide the Union Budget 2026-27?
questions.explanation: The three Kartavyas are Sustain Economic Growth, Fulfill Aspirations, and Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas.

questions.q: Which pillar of growth focuses on the long-term stability of economic and financial systems?
options: Ensuring long-term security and stability in economic and financial systems
Delivering infrastructure development across the country
Rejuvenating legacy industrial sectors to boost productivity and competitiveness
questions.explanation: The pillar on ensuring long-term security and stability covers economic and financial systems.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Day on which the budget was tabled   ->   D. Regional growth and urban development
II. Building where the budget was prepared   ->   C. Manufacturing in seven strategic sectors
III. Pillar for developing city economic regions   ->   B. Sunday
IV. Pillar for scaling up manufacturing   ->   A. Kartavya Bhawan
questions.explanation: The budget was tabled on Sunday, prepared in Kartavya Bhawan, and the two pillars aim at regional growth and manufacturing respectively.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Ensuring long-term security and stability in economic and financial systems is one of the six pillars of growth.
II. The first-ever Union Budget was tabled on a Saturday, a Parliamentary first.
III. Fulfill Aspirations is one of the three Kartavyas.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the budget was tabled on a Sunday, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Union Budget 2026-27 are correct?
I. Sustain Economic Growth is one of the three Kartavyas.
II. The first-ever Union Budget was tabled on a Monday.
III. The budget was prepared in the Kartavya Bhawan.
IV. Developing city economic regions is one of the six pillars of growth.
questions.explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct, while statement II is wrong because the budget was tabled on a Sunday.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The first-ever Union Budget was tabled on a Sunday.
Reason (R): Creating champion MSMEs is one of the six pillars of growth.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the MSME pillar does not explain why the budget was tabled on a Sunday.

questions.q: Which pillar's goal is to drive regional growth and urban development? (two words)
questions.explanation: The pillar on developing city economic regions aims to drive regional growth and urban development.

questions.q: Name the newly inaugurated building in which the Union Budget 2026-27 was prepared. (two words)

questions.q: What does the pillar on rejuvenating legacy industrial sectors aim to boost, along with competitiveness? (one word)

questions.q: Which national vision is the Union Budget 2026-27 anchored in? (two words)

quizzes.title: Agriculture and Women-led MCQ
quizzes.passage: The budget set out measures for agriculture, services and women-led development, which it presented as separate parts of its agenda. For farmers, it proposed an AI-based platform that gives access to agricultural resources in several languages. It also announced special support for crops that can help farmers diversify into higher-margin plantation crops. The budget set a goal for certain Indian farm exports to earn a stronger global brand, which is intended to enhance export realisation. In services, the budget proposes Content Creator Labs in schools and colleges to build a talent pipeline for a booming sector. The budget also promotes the Orange Economy, which is grouped under services, technology and tourism. For women-led development, the budget proposed SHE Marts, through which women's self-help groups can sell products directly. It also proposed a girls' hostel in each district, to help more female students stay in science, technology, engineering and mathematics courses. Each of these proposals is presented as a separate initiative within the budget. The budget describes these measures as steps toward growth in agriculture, services and women-led development. Taken together, they are part of the government's wider growth agenda for the year ahead. Each of these areas is discussed separately in the budget, and each has its own set of measures.

questions.q: Special support was announced for cultivating which set of crops to help farmers diversify into high-margin plantation crops?
options: Sandalwood, agar trees, walnuts and almonds
questions.explanation: The booklet names sandalwood, agar trees, walnuts and almonds as the crops receiving special support.

questions.q: By which year is Global Brand Status targeted for Indian cashew and cocoa?
questions.explanation: The government set a target of Global Brand Status for Indian cashew and cocoa by 2030.

questions.q: The Content Creator Labs are meant to build a talent pipeline for which sector?
options: AVGC (Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics)
questions.explanation: The labs build a talent pipeline for the AVGC sector, which covers animation, VFX, gaming and comics.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Green economy   ->   B. Sustainable, low-carbon, energy-efficient industries
II. Blue economy   ->   D. Ageing population and senior services
III. White economy   ->   A. Marine and ocean-based activities
IV. Silver economy   ->   C. Health and social care sector
questions.explanation: Green economy relates to sustainable industries, Blue to marine activities, White to health care and Silver to senior services.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Special support is announced for sandalwood, agar trees, walnuts and almonds.
II. SHE Marts are to be run by private companies for profit.
III. Global Brand Status is targeted for Indian cashew and cocoa.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I and III match the booklet, while SHE Marts are described as community-owned retail outlets for women's SHGs.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Orange Economy are correct?
I. The term Orange Economy was coined in a 2013 work.
II. Its value comes mainly from physical production.
III. Content Creator Labs are to be set up in 500 schools.
IV. Live entertainment such as theatre is among its key sectors.
questions.explanation: Statements I and IV are correct, while the Orange Economy derives value from intellectual property rather than physical production.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Orange Economy's value comes mainly from intellectual property and cultural expression.
Reason (R): The Orange Economy is driven by knowledge and creativity rather than physical production.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and R restates why the value of the Orange Economy comes from ideas rather than physical goods, which explains A.

questions.q: The AI-based farm platform in the budget integrates which set of portals, named in the booklet? (one word)

questions.q: How many schools are to host Content Creator Labs? (number in digits)

quizzes.title: Budget Process and Parliament MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Constitution requires the government to present an annual statement of its estimated receipts and expenditure for each financial year before both Houses of Parliament. The word budget itself does not appear anywhere in the Constitution, although the annual statement is treated as the budget. The process has several stages. It begins with presentation of the statement, followed by general discussion and scrutiny by departmental committees. Then Parliament votes on demands for grants, passes an appropriation bill and passes a finance bill. The preparation of the statement is handled by a division of the finance ministry, which works with other ministries and a government policy body. Money bills and finance bills follow special procedures, and the two houses of Parliament have different roles in them. Budgets have been presented in India for well over a century, and the earliest one came before independence. The annual statement sets out the government's expected revenue and spending for the year ahead, and it also records the actual receipts and expenditure of the closing year. The budget is presented in Parliament on a date fixed for the purpose. Parliament examines the statement in a series of stages each year, and each stage has its own role in the process.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution requires the annual financial statement to be laid before Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 112 in Part V requires the annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure.

questions.q: The Budget Division that prepares the Union Budget belongs to which department?
questions.explanation: The Budget Division sits in the Department of Economic Affairs of the Ministry of Finance.

questions.q: In which year was the Railway Budget merged with the Union Budget?
questions.explanation: The Railway Budget, presented separately for 92 years, was merged with the Union Budget in 2017.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Money/Finance Bill involving taxation   ->   B. Presented separately for 92 years
II. Rajya Sabha   ->   A. Introduced only in Lok Sabha
III. Railway Budget   ->   C. Presented by R.K. Shanmukham Chetty
IV. First post-independence Union Budget   ->   D. Must return a Money/Finance Bill within 14 days
questions.explanation: Money bills start in Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha returns them within 14 days, the Railway Budget was presented separately, and Chetty presented the first post-independence budget.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Budget Division works with NITI Aayog and ministries in preparing the budget.
II. Rajya Sabha has the power to vote on demands for grants.
III. The budget announcement has been made on the first working day of February since 2017.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while Rajya Sabha has no power to vote on demands for grants.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Union Budget are correct?
I. India's first budget was presented on 7 April 1860.
II. Part A of the Budget Speech deals with a general economic survey.
III. Part B of the Budget Speech relates to the general economic survey.
IV. Money bills can be introduced in Rajya Sabha.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while Part B covers taxation proposals and Money bills are introduced in Lok Sabha.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Money/Finance Bills involving taxation are introduced only in Lok Sabha.
Reason (R): Rajya Sabha must return a Money/Finance Bill within 14 days.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the 14-day return rule does not explain why such bills start in Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution (Part V) is the annual financial statement provided for? (number)
questions.explanation: Article 112 in Part V provides for the annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure.

questions.q: Which division of the Department of Economic Affairs prepares the Union Budget? (two words)
questions.explanation: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs prepares the budget with NITI Aayog and ministries.

questions.q: In which year was the Railway Budget merged with the Union Budget? (year)
questions.explanation: The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in 2017 after being presented separately for 92 years.

questions.q: Who presented India's first budget on 7 April 1860, as Finance Member of the India Council? (full name)
questions.explanation: James Wilson, Finance Member of the India Council, presented India's first budget in 1860.

questions.q: For how many years was the Railway Budget presented separately before its merger? (number)
questions.explanation: The Railway Budget was presented separately for 92 years until it was merged in 2017.

questions.q: Who presented the first Union Budget after independence, on 26 November 1947? (surname)
questions.explanation: Sir R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first post-independence Union Budget on 26 November 1947.

questions.q: Which house of Parliament must return a Money/Finance Bill within 14 days? (two words)
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha must return a Money/Finance Bill to Lok Sabha within 14 days.
